world.title: Netanyahu denies UAE warned of October 7 attack
world.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office denied a Haaretz report saying UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan warned him shortly before the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack that Hamas was planning a major operation against Israel. The report, excerpted from a forthcoming book by Haaretz journalists, said
world.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office denied a Haaretz report saying UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan warned him shortly before the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack that Hamas was planning a major operation against Israel. The report, excerpted from a forthcoming book by Haaretz journalists, said the UAE leader spoke with Netanyahu about 10 days before the attack and raised concerns about then Hamas leader in Gaza Yahya Sinwar’s plans. Haaretz reported that bin Zayed warned the operation could cause bloodshed, destabilize the region and undermine the Abraham Accords, while Netanyahu responded with “relative calm,” said Israel was prepared for any scenario and suggested a possible attack was more likely from the occupied West Bank. Netanyahu’s office called the report “an absolute lie” and said the UAE gave no warning before October 7. The UAE Foreign Ministry did not explicitly confirm the account, but said it shares intelligence with the appropriate entities when necessary. Israeli opposition leaders called Netanyahu unfit to serve after the report, which emerged during Israel’s election campaign.

world.title: Iceland summons US envoy over Trump
world.summary: Iceland summoned the US ambassador after President Trump posted a Truth Social image on Monday showing the United States, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean covered in the US flag and labeled “United States of America”. Iceland’s foreign minister called in the newly appointed US ambas
world.content: Iceland summoned the US ambassador after President Trump posted a Truth Social image on Monday showing the United States, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean covered in the US flag and labeled “United States of America”. Iceland’s foreign minister called in the newly appointed US ambassador for an explanation, while Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir condemned the post. France 24 described the image as AI-generated and said Mexico reiterated its sovereignty and Denmark objected to the depiction of Greenland after the post. The New York Times linked Iceland’s forceful reaction to the country’s recent vote against opening talks to join the European Union.

world.title: Houthis strike Saudi cities, wounding 73 people
world.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding 73 people and setting oil installations on fire in an expansion of the six-month-old Middle East war. The strikes used ballistic missiles and drones and hit Saudi territory, including energy facilities and civilian infrastruc
world.content: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding 73 people and setting oil installations on fire in an expansion of the six-month-old Middle East war. The strikes used ballistic missiles and drones and hit Saudi territory, including energy facilities and civilian infrastructure, temporarily halting operations at some energy sites. U.S. forces also struck multiple Iranian tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps after Iranian attempts to hit a U.S. Navy warship, a U.S. official said, resuming U.S. attacks on Iran after a two-day pause. Iranian media reported that a U.S. missile hit an Iranian tanker 4 miles from Kharg Island and that a second tanker was attacked near Jask in the Gulf of Oman; the IRGC then threatened to target oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports and warned crews to evacuate. The Houthis said they had launched a broad operation deep into Saudi territory, while Saudi authorities vowed to retaliate. The strikes followed Houthi accusations on September 7 that Riyadh had carried out attacks around Yemen, including the deadly bombardment of a prison.
world.image_alt: Houthis strike Saudi cities, wounding 73 people

world.title: Rubio seeks closer security, trade ties with Colombia
world.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella in Barranquilla on September 8, starting a three-country Latin America tour focused on security and economic cooperation. Rubio pledged to restore U.S.-Colombia ties and said Washington saw an opening for relations to enter a stronger
world.content: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella in Barranquilla on September 8, starting a three-country Latin America tour focused on security and economic cooperation. Rubio pledged to restore U.S.-Colombia ties and said Washington saw an opening for relations to enter a stronger phase after De la Espriella’s election and recent moves to deepen military cooperation with the United States. The trip includes Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. Rubio said President Trump’s administration hopes to complete trade deals with the three countries soon. In Colombia, Rubio’s agenda included drug-trafficking groups, trade, critical minerals, civil nuclear cooperation and questions about Bogotá’s ties with China, including participation in the Belt and Road Initiative and Chinese investment in critical infrastructure.
world.image_alt: Rubio seeks closer security, trade ties with Colombia

world.title: Russia strikes Kyiv and Ukraine-Moldova border, killing at least seven
world.summary: Russia struck Kyiv with drones and missiles on Tuesday after a three-day halt in attacks on the Ukrainian and Russian capitals during visits by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. The attack killed five people in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Officials said the Kyiv strike caused fires across several dist
world.content: Russia struck Kyiv with drones and missiles on Tuesday after a three-day halt in attacks on the Ukrainian and Russian capitals during visits by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. The attack killed five people in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Officials said the Kyiv strike caused fires across several districts and damaged at least 14 high-rise buildings, a dormitory, a school, a clinic, warehouses and other sites. During a live United News broadcast, a Russian drone also damaged the Kyiv building of the Ukrainian television channel We Are Ukraine, injuring five people, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Ukrainian authorities said Russian drones hit a Ukraine-Moldova border crossing in the southern Odesa region on Wednesday, killing two people and injuring others. Kushner and Witkoff left Kyiv on Sunday after talks with Zelenskyy, following discussions in Moscow. After the Moscow talks, the Kremlin said it did not rule out resuming three-way negotiations involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The BBC cited officials as saying a separate attack on a passenger train in southern Ukraine killed a female employee.
world.image_alt: Russia strikes Kyiv and Ukraine-Moldova border, killing at least seven

world.title: New York releases 170,000 post-9/11 toxic-air records
world.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani released more than 170,000 previously unreleased records on Sept. 8 about air quality after the September 11, 2001, attacks, saying the files show the city did not disclose everything it knew about toxic air around Ground Zero. The records include air-quality reports and communications amo
world.content: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani released more than 170,000 previously unreleased records on Sept. 8 about air quality after the September 11, 2001, attacks, saying the files show the city did not disclose everything it knew about toxic air around Ground Zero. The records include air-quality reports and communications among city officials, and suggest authorities knew of health risks while people were receiving public assurances that the air was safe to breathe. The release precedes the 25th anniversary of the attacks, which killed 2,977 people in the United States, most of them in the collapse of the Twin Towers in New York. In the years since, more than 9,400 people have died from illnesses linked to exposure in the area, according to a federal medical monitoring program cited by AFP.
world.image_alt: New York releases 170,000 post-9/11 toxic-air records

world.title: Trump and Putin discuss Ukraine peace efforts
world.summary: President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed the war in Ukraine in an hour-long phone call on September 8. The Kremlin described the exchange as “extremely frank,” “constructive and candid,” and focused on efforts to end the fighting. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Trump told Putin he wanted a swift e
world.content: President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed the war in Ukraine in an hour-long phone call on September 8. The Kremlin described the exchange as “extremely frank,” “constructive and candid,” and focused on efforts to end the fighting. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Trump told Putin he wanted a swift end to the war and saw ending it as a condition for fully restoring U.S.-Russia relations. El País reported that Trump offered “significant economic benefits” in exchange for ending the conflict. The call followed weekend trips to Moscow and Kyiv by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who held separate talks with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Washington pushed for renewed face-to-face talks between Moscow and Kyiv. Ushakov said Putin praised U.S. mediation efforts, suggested steps Washington could take, and told Trump Russia had no aggressive plans toward Europe. U.S. officials had not commented on the substance of the call when Meduza published its report.
world.image_alt: Trump and Putin discuss Ukraine peace efforts

world.title: UK air traffic control issue cancels more than 1,000 flights
world.summary: Britain's air traffic control provider NATS said a technical issue in its flight data processing system disrupted flights across UK airports on Tuesday, forcing more than 1,000 cancellations and delaying hundreds more at major hubs including Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester, Stansted and Birmingham, as well as airports in
world.content: Britain's air traffic control provider NATS said a technical issue in its flight data processing system disrupted flights across UK airports on Tuesday, forcing more than 1,000 cancellations and delaying hundreds more at major hubs including Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester, Stansted and Birmingham, as well as airports in Scotland. NATS said it had resolved the issue and that safety was not compromised, but recovery continued after aircraft and crews were left out of position. Disruption continued on Wednesday, when Flightradar24 said 177 scheduled flights to and from UK airports had already been cancelled, nearly all at London Heathrow. Heathrow said departures had resumed after the issue forced it to suspend arrivals, while airports and airlines warned passengers to check flight status as carriers worked through backlogs. The UK transport secretary, Heidi Alexander, said she was seeking assurances that lessons would be learned and that aviation support systems were fit for purpose, and was expected to meet NATS chief executive Martin Rolfe on Wednesday. Rolfe told Sky News he accepted "full responsibility" and said NATS had not yet completed its investigation into the cause.
world.image_alt: UK air traffic control issue cancels more than 1,000 flights

business.title: LIV Golf files for Chapter 11 with at least $500m in liabilities
business.summary: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey on Tuesday, seeking a court-supervised restructuring after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund ended its multibillion-dollar backing earlier this year. Court filings estimate LIV's assets at $100 million to $500 million and
business.content: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey on Tuesday, seeking a court-supervised restructuring after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund ended its multibillion-dollar backing earlier this year. Court filings estimate LIV's assets at $100 million to $500 million and liabilities at $500 million to $1 billion, with at least 1,000 creditors and more than $45 million owed to 14 current and former players listed among the 30 largest unsecured claims. The league said it has a restructuring agreement with BC Partners Credit and plans to shift toward a majority player-owned model, while PIF has agreed to provide $49.6 million in debtor-in-possession financing during the case. LIV said it aims to emerge from Chapter 11 and begin a new version of the league in early 2027, but has not announced definitive decisions on the 2027 schedule or individual events.
business.image_alt: LIV Golf files for Chapter 11 with at least $500m in liabilities

business.title: NTSB says Amazon cargo pilots tried to abort deadly Miami landing
business.summary: National Transportation Safety Board investigators said flight data indicate the pilots of Amazon Air Flight 7598 may have initiated a go-around seconds before the Boeing 767-300 overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The aircraft, operated by 21 Air for Ama
business.content: National Transportation Safety Board investigators said flight data indicate the pilots of Amazon Air Flight 7598 may have initiated a go-around seconds before the Boeing 767-300 overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The aircraft, operated by 21 Air for Amazon, hit a van used by an airline cleaning contractor and then a Toyota SUV, killing five people in the van and injuring five others. NTSB data released Tuesday showed the nose landing gear and right main landing gear touched down about 30 seconds before the flight-data recording ended, the left main landing gear touched down 19 seconds before the end, and the brakes were then released as the throttles increased to settings consistent with a go-around. Investigators said the throttles returned to idle and the brakes were reapplied about 11 seconds before the recording ended, with no flight-recorder indication that speed brakes or thrust reversers deployed during the incident.
business.image_alt: NTSB says Amazon cargo pilots tried to abort deadly Miami landing

business.title: UK air traffic fault cancels more than 1,300 flights
business.summary: A technical fault at UK air traffic control provider Nats disrupted flights across major British airports on Tuesday and left airlines working through cancellations and delays on Wednesday. Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted were among the affected airports, while Dublin and other airports in Ireland also repor
business.content: A technical fault at UK air traffic control provider Nats disrupted flights across major British airports on Tuesday and left airlines working through cancellations and delays on Wednesday. Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted were among the affected airports, while Dublin and other airports in Ireland also reported knock-on disruption. Aviation data providers gave different cancellation totals: Cirium counted more than 1,750 cancellations on Tuesday and 153 on Wednesday, while Flightradar24 put Tuesday cancellations at about 1,300 and Wednesday cancellations at 177, nearly all at Heathrow. Nats said the problem was in its flight processing system, implemented a fix, and later said the system was operating normally while teams worked to clear the backlog. Chief executive Martin Rolfe apologised and said Nats had not completed its investigation into the cause, while Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander summoned him to a Wednesday meeting and was expected to tell MPs that a cyberattack was categorically not the cause. EasyJet made 200 cancellations and British Airways more than 100, according to the BBC, while Ryanair said the outage affected around 150,000 of its passengers and led it to cancel more than 200 flights.
business.image_alt: UK air traffic fault cancels more than 1,300 flights

business.title: Hunter Biden launches $LAPTOP crypto token on Base
business.summary: Hunter Biden is launching a political meme coin called $LAPTOP on September 9 on Coinbase’s Base network, a reference to the laptop controversy from the 2020 U.S. presidential campaign. Biden previewed the token on X with the ticker and launch date alongside footage of media commentary about the laptop story. The token
business.content: Hunter Biden is launching a political meme coin called $LAPTOP on September 9 on Coinbase’s Base network, a reference to the laptop controversy from the 2020 U.S. presidential campaign. Biden previewed the token on X with the ticker and launch date alongside footage of media commentary about the laptop story. The token has a fixed supply of 1 billion coins; Biden and other founders will hold 30% of the supply, with reports saying lockup terms include six months followed by releases over about two years. Another 20% is allocated to airdrops that include wallets that lost money on President Trump’s $TRUMP meme coin, Biden’s Substack subscribers and a mailing list linked to video journalist Andrew Callaghan. The launch drew criticism from crypto traders before trading began. Kraken deleted a promotional post, and Base founder Jesse Pollak said the network did not help design or promote the token. Biden defended the project ahead of the launch by framing it as an effort to take ownership of the laptop controversy, while project materials say the token has no utility or ownership rights and warn that digital-asset prices can fall to zero.
business.image_alt: Hunter Biden launches $LAPTOP crypto token on Base

business.title: Meta launches Muse AI agent for U.S. users
business.summary: Meta launched Muse on Tuesday, making the personal AI agent available to U.S. adults through a dedicated app, WhatsApp and the web, with smart-glasses support planned later. The company says Muse can connect to user-selected apps and services to send emails, book travel, make payments, shop online, fill out forms and w
business.content: Meta launched Muse on Tuesday, making the personal AI agent available to U.S. adults through a dedicated app, WhatsApp and the web, with smart-glasses support planned later. The company says Muse can connect to user-selected apps and services to send emails, book travel, make payments, shop online, fill out forms and work on longer projects such as exercise plans or setting up a business. Muse has a free tier and paid plans at $20 and $100 a month for heavier use. Meta describes it as an agent that can act on a user's behalf, rather than a chatbot limited to answering questions. The product could put more activity such as payments, email and shopping inside Meta's systems while the company faces scrutiny over privacy and safety, including a recently reported $18 billion multistate settlement over social media harms. Meta says Muse runs in a dedicated secure virtual machine, lets users choose which apps and services it can access, and permits them to withdraw permissions at any time.
business.image_alt: Meta launches Muse AI agent for U.S. users

business.title: Brent oil reaches $100 after Gulf attacks
business.summary: Brent crude hit $100 a barrel on Wednesday after renewed attacks around Gulf shipping routes and Saudi energy facilities intensified concerns about Middle East supply disruptions. Earlier Asian trading put Brent near $99.33-$99.49 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate around $94.34-$94.63 after a fourth consecutive
business.content: Brent crude hit $100 a barrel on Wednesday after renewed attacks around Gulf shipping routes and Saudi energy facilities intensified concerns about Middle East supply disruptions. Earlier Asian trading put Brent near $99.33-$99.49 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate around $94.34-$94.63 after a fourth consecutive session of gains. U.S. Central Command said American forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers on Sept. 8 after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard twice targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles; the U.S. said the warship evaded the attacks and no American personnel were harmed. Iran then said it fired missiles at a U.S. base in Jordan and attacked two U.S. vessels, eight oil tankers and 10 other ships near the Strait of Hormuz, while Jordan said it intercepted 18 of 20 ballistic missiles and reported no casualties. The price move followed Houthi attacks on Saudi cities and energy sites, with reports of fires and halted operations at facilities in southern Saudi Arabia. Analysts cited a growing risk premium tied to threats to shipping and infrastructure, while Goldman Sachs raised oil forecasts and said Brent could exceed $120 if attacks on Middle East shipping intensify.
business.image_alt: Brent oil reaches $100 after Gulf attacks

business.title: Mistral raises €3 billion in Samsung-led AI round
business.summary: French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI said Tuesday it raised €3 billion in a Series D round led by Samsung Electronics, valuing the Paris-based startup at more than €21 billion. Mistral called the round the largest equity fundraising ever completed by a European technology company. The Scaleup Europe Fund m
business.content: French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI said Tuesday it raised €3 billion in a Series D round led by Samsung Electronics, valuing the Paris-based startup at more than €21 billion. Mistral called the round the largest equity fundraising ever completed by a European technology company. The Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT and existing investor PSG Equity joined Samsung as co-leads. The company said it will use the money to expand computing capacity, build infrastructure, accelerate commercial growth and widen its international footprint. Mistral has positioned its open-weight models and infrastructure strategy around customers that want control over data, models, computing power and production systems instead of depending on closed AI ecosystems. Mistral’s valuation has risen from €11.7 billion after a 2025 Series C round led by ASML to more than €21 billion, nearly doubling in a year. The company remains far smaller than OpenAI; several reports put OpenAI’s latest financing valuation at about $852 billion. Mistral says it operates in 20 countries and serves more than 125 large customers, including Airbus, ASML and HSBC.
business.image_alt: Mistral raises €3 billion in Samsung-led AI round

business.title: Apple expected to launch foldable iPhone under Ternus
business.summary: Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone at its “Surprise and Shine” event on Sept. 9 at its Cupertino, California, headquarters, its first major product showcase under CEO John Ternus, who succeeded Tim Cook on Sept. 1. The device is expected to open like a passport, marking the iPhone’s biggest form-fact
business.content: Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone at its “Surprise and Shine” event on Sept. 9 at its Cupertino, California, headquarters, its first major product showcase under CEO John Ternus, who succeeded Tim Cook on Sept. 1. The device is expected to open like a passport, marking the iPhone’s biggest form-factor change since Apple introduced the smartphone in 2007. The launch would test demand for a high-priced device as iPhone upgrades slow in a mature U.S. market, where Americans own about 158 million iPhones, more than half of U.S. adults. Price estimates range from above $2,000 to more than $2,500, with Bloomberg-linked reports saying some larger-storage configurations could approach $3,000 as component costs rise. Apple also faces investor scrutiny over artificial intelligence after analysts said the company has trailed rivals in generative AI and needs to show progress on Siri.
business.image_alt: Apple expected to launch foldable iPhone under Ternus

science.title: Slime mould studies prompt debate over intelligence
science.summary: A Guardian long read examined a scientific dispute over whether organisms such as slime moulds should be described as “intelligent,” focusing on research into Physarum polycephalum and biological and philosophical arguments over intelligence in organisms long treated as simple. The article traces the debate through Tos
science.content: A Guardian long read examined a scientific dispute over whether organisms such as slime moulds should be described as “intelligent,” focusing on research into Physarum polycephalum and biological and philosophical arguments over intelligence in organisms long treated as simple. The article traces the debate through Toshiyuki Nakagaki, who encountered a lemon-yellow slime mould in a petri dish as an undergraduate in Hokkaido about 40 years ago and later became a leading researcher in the field. Physarum polycephalum moves at about 1 cm an hour, senses meals of bacteria or other microbes, extends thin protoplasmic structures toward food, digests it, and then forages farther or withdraws into the organism. The Guardian contrasted that behavior with descriptions from 1895 and later that called slime moulds “a simple mass of protoplasm” and “among the most simple of organisms”.
science.image_alt: Slime mould studies prompt debate over intelligence

science.title: Study projects drylands could exceed 40% of land
science.summary: A study published in Environmental Research Letters estimates that drylands could expand to more than 40% of Earth's land surface by 2100, revising projections by accounting for how rising carbon dioxide changes plant water use. The research, led by the Chinese Academy of Forestry, used updated climate models to assess
science.content: A study published in Environmental Research Letters estimates that drylands could expand to more than 40% of Earth's land surface by 2100, revising projections by accounting for how rising carbon dioxide changes plant water use. The research, led by the Chinese Academy of Forestry, used updated climate models to assess global aridity patterns. The study estimates drylands now cover about 38.5% of land and could expand by roughly 2.37 million square kilometers to about 40.3% by the end of the century. Researchers said higher atmospheric CO2 can cause plants to partially close stomata, reducing water loss and slowing projected dryland expansion compared with some earlier estimates. They said the change does not remove risks tied to water scarcity, ecosystem degradation and desertification.
science.image_alt: Study projects drylands could exceed 40% of land

science.title: Researchers describe new frog and owl species
science.summary: Scientists described two vertebrates as new species in separate 2026 publications: Pristimantis milpe, a rain frog from western Ecuador, and Bubo jalca, a horned owl from northern Peru. The Ecuadorian frog had been classified since 1980 under a name that researchers now say belongs to a different lineage that diverged
science.content: Scientists described two vertebrates as new species in separate 2026 publications: Pristimantis milpe, a rain frog from western Ecuador, and Bubo jalca, a horned owl from northern Peru. The Ecuadorian frog had been classified since 1980 under a name that researchers now say belongs to a different lineage that diverged from it about 24 million years ago, according to a published phylogeny. The frog, one of the most widely distributed Pristimantis species in the Ecuadorian Chocó, is locally abundant and conspicuous because males call loudly from bromeliads at night. The owl inhabits jalca, a cold, high-elevation grassland and cloud-forest habitat in the Huancabamba Depression, and researchers distinguished it from its closest relative mainly by vocalization rather than plumage or body measurements.
science.image_alt: Researchers describe new frog and owl species

science.title: Dementia research highlights prevention, depression and statins
science.summary: Recent dementia research and guidance focused on prevention policy, early biological warning signs and possible risk reduction after type 2 diabetes diagnosis. The World Health Organization issued updated recommendations after a 2024 Lancet review estimated that 14 potentially modifiable risk factors are associated wit
science.content: Recent dementia research and guidance focused on prevention policy, early biological warning signs and possible risk reduction after type 2 diabetes diagnosis. The World Health Organization issued updated recommendations after a 2024 Lancet review estimated that 14 potentially modifiable risk factors are associated with up to 45% of dementia cases at a population level. A JNeurosci study using Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data found that faster tau accumulation was associated with worsening depressive symptoms in older adults who remained cognitively healthy. Researchers did not detect the same relationship among participants with mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer’s disease. Separately, a nationwide Danish study of more than 132,000 people found that those who started statins within a year of a type 2 diabetes diagnosis had a 15% lower relative risk of dementia over 10 years compared with those who did not start statins. The statin research was presented at ESC Congress 2026 and published in The Lancet Regional Health - Europe. The tau-depression study did not establish that tau directly causes depression. WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the new dementia guidance gives countries evidence-based recommendations they can apply immediately.
science.image_alt: Dementia research highlights prevention, depression and statins

science.title: Physicists observe Einstein gravitational effect in quantum atoms
science.summary: Physicists reported the first direct observation of a long-predicted gravitational effect in a falling quantum object, using ultracold atoms to test an idea rooted in Einstein’s equivalence principle. Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, the University of Ulm and the University of Oxford led the work, published Sept. 2
science.content: Physicists reported the first direct observation of a long-predicted gravitational effect in a falling quantum object, using ultracold atoms to test an idea rooted in Einstein’s equivalence principle. Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, the University of Ulm and the University of Oxford led the work, published Sept. 2 in Science Advances. In the experiment, researchers split an atom’s quantum wave so that one branch remained held in place while the other fell freely under Earth’s gravity, then recombined the paths to measure a tiny phase difference. The measured effect matched predictions from extending the equivalence principle to quantum behavior under the conditions tested.
science.image_alt: Physicists observe Einstein gravitational effect in quantum atoms

science.title: Hubble and Webb show distant icy objects preserve clues to the past
science.summary: Scientists used NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope together for the first time to study trans-Neptunian objects, small icy bodies that orbit the Sun beyond Neptune. The study examined 27 newly detected objects that are unusually small and faint, and found fewer small TNOs than researchers expe
science.content: Scientists used NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope together for the first time to study trans-Neptunian objects, small icy bodies that orbit the Sun beyond Neptune. The study examined 27 newly detected objects that are unusually small and faint, and found fewer small TNOs than researchers expected. The observations showed that the small objects’ colors matched relationships seen among larger TNOs, suggesting their surfaces still preserve clues about where they formed despite long exposure to collisions and space conditions. The team also measured sizes and orbits for the sample, using the data to study Kuiper Belt dynamics and the mass distribution left from the early solar system.
science.image_alt: Hubble and Webb show distant icy objects preserve clues to the past

science.title: Researchers study photon from 2022 gamma-ray burst
science.summary: Researchers are examining an unusually energetic photon detected from a massive 2022 gamma-ray burst, one that current physics says should have been absorbed before reaching Earth. Phys.org reported that the photon traveled more than 2 billion light-years, making its arrival at Earth the central puzzle in a new study b
science.content: Researchers are examining an unusually energetic photon detected from a massive 2022 gamma-ray burst, one that current physics says should have been absorbed before reaching Earth. Phys.org reported that the photon traveled more than 2 billion light-years, making its arrival at Earth the central puzzle in a new study by Giorgio Galanti of INAF and Marco Roncadelli of INFN. Phys.org reported that the study has been accepted for publication in Physical Review Letters. Available descriptions of the article do not specify the proposed mechanism, but they describe the finding as a challenge to established expectations about how such high-energy photons interact with matter and radiation across intergalactic distances.
science.image_alt: Researchers study photon from 2022 gamma-ray burst

science.title: NASA Genesis capsule crash revisited 22 years later
science.summary: Science Blog and Space.com revisited NASA’s Genesis sample-return mission on the 22nd anniversary of its Sept. 8, 2004, crash in the Utah desert, where the capsule struck the ground with its parachutes undeployed after returning solar-wind collectors from space. Science Blog, citing NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory rep
science.content: Science Blog and Space.com revisited NASA’s Genesis sample-return mission on the 22nd anniversary of its Sept. 8, 2004, crash in the Utah desert, where the capsule struck the ground with its parachutes undeployed after returning solar-wind collectors from space. Science Blog, citing NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory report, said the capsule hit the Utah Test and Training Range at 311 kilometers per hour, or 193 mph. Genesis carried wafers of sapphire, silicon and other ultrapure materials that collected solar-wind atoms during more than two years in space, but the impact broke much of the collector material and exposed it to terrestrial contamination. NASA’s Mishap Investigation Board found that an erroneous design had left four gravity switches in two redundant avionics units installed upside down, preventing the deceleration signal needed to start parachute deployment. Scientists later recovered useful measurements from the damaged collectors.
science.image_alt: NASA Genesis capsule crash revisited 22 years later

sports.title: Buccaneers lock up Baker Mayfield with $165 million extension
sports.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and quarterback Baker Mayfield agreed Tuesday to a three-year, $165 million contract extension that prevents him from reaching free agency after the 2026 season, according to ESPN and The Associated Press; CBS Sports and WTSP said the team announced the deal. The extension averages $55 million
sports.content: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and quarterback Baker Mayfield agreed Tuesday to a three-year, $165 million contract extension that prevents him from reaching free agency after the 2026 season, according to ESPN and The Associated Press; CBS Sports and WTSP said the team announced the deal. The extension averages $55 million per year and is the largest contract in Buccaneers franchise history, making Mayfield the highest-paid player in team history. The agreement came after Mayfield entered the final season of the three-year, $100 million deal he signed in March 2024 and after contract talks appeared to pause around the start of training camp. Mayfield, the No. 1 pick in the 2018 NFL draft, became Tampa Bay's starter after replacing Tom Brady in 2023, earned Pro Bowl selections in each of his first two Buccaneers seasons and led the team to consecutive NFC South titles. Tampa Bay opens the 2026 season Sunday at Cincinnati against the Bengals.
sports.image_alt: Buccaneers lock up Baker Mayfield with $165 million extension

sports.title: Aaron Judge returns as Yankees beat Rockies 5-3

sports.content: Aaron Judge returned to the New York Yankees' lineup Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium after a 99-day absence caused by a fractured right rib, starting in right field and batting third against the Colorado Rockies. The Yankees won 5-3, with Judge going 0-for-3 with two strikeouts and a flyout before exiting after six innings under a planned workload limit. New York’s victory was its 82nd win and clinched the club’s 34th consecutive winning season, the second-longest such streak in the four major North American sports behind the Yankees’ 39 straight winning seasons from 1926-64. Heliot Ramos replaced Judge in right field and hit a three-run homer in the eighth inning that proved decisive, while Cam Schlittler struck out 10 over seven innings.

sports.title: NCAA lets Michigan win stand after MAC appeal

sports.content: The NCAA said Michigan’s 13-12 win over Western Michigan will stand after the Mid-American Conference appealed the finish and asked the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and College Football Playoff administrators to recognize Western Michigan as the winner for ranking and selection purposes. Michigan won Saturday night in Ann Arbor when quarterback Bryce Underwood threw a final-play Hail Mary to JJ Buchanan after replay officials restored one second to the clock following an earlier incomplete deep pass. MAC Commissioner Jon Steinbrecher said the conference changed course after further review because it believed the replay crew used a clock embedded in the Big Ten replay system rather than the program-feed clock required by established replay protocol. The Big Ten said it stood by its postgame explanation and the determination made by replay officials, while the NCAA said its playing rules have no protocol for overturning a completed game and that the FBS Oversight Committee lacks authority to do so. The MAC also asked the CFP to consider Western Michigan as the actual winner during rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations. Separately, ESPN reported that the NCAA issued new guidance on a “standard timing protocol” after the Michigan finish, addressing replay reviews that require time to be restored.

sports.content: Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Aaron Donald will not travel to Melbourne and will be inactive for the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers, delaying the defensive tackle’s first NFL game since the 2023 season. The Rams decided after Donald returned from retirement in late August that he would continue his conditioning ramp-up in Los Angeles rather than make the long trip to Australia. McVay said the 35-year-old is working his way back into game shape and that the 16-hour flight was a factor in keeping him in Los Angeles to continue preparing. The Rams and 49ers will play at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Friday morning local time, with kickoff listed by ABC at 10:35 a.m. AEST.

sports.content: Newcastle United reached the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 1-0 win over Millwall at The Den on Tuesday, September 8, after Joe Willock scored in the 81st minute. The result sent Matthias Jaissle’s Premier League side past a Championship opponent that kept the tie scoreless deep into the second half before Willock turned in Lewis Hall’s ball across the six-yard box. Millwall nearly went ahead shortly before the goal when Tairyk Arconte struck the post, but Newcastle held on for a clean sheet. Jaissle praised his players’ response, while reports said Millwall were missing several injured players and kept the match level until the 81st minute.

sports.content: Aston Villa opened their 2026-27 Champions League league-phase campaign with a 3-2 away win over Club Brugge at Jan Breydel Stadium on September 8, earning their first victory of the season. John McGinn put Villa ahead in the 11th minute, Hugo Vetlesen equalised in the 19th, Emiliano Buendía restored the lead in the 22nd and Nicolas Jackson scored his first Villa goal in the 43rd to send Unai Emery’s side in 3-1 up at half-time. Club Brugge cut the deficit in the 61st minute when Nicolò Tresoldi converted a penalty after Aaron Wan-Bissaka handled in the area, and the Belgian side kept pressure on Villa in the closing stages. Villa held on after entering the match without scoring in their first three Premier League games.

sports.content: Real Madrid opened its 2026-27 Champions League league-phase campaign with a 2-1 win over Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabéu on Tuesday, giving José Mourinho a winning European start in his second spell as the club’s manager. Kylian Mbappé scored in the 14th minute after Brahim Díaz seized on an Inter mistake, and Federico Valverde doubled the lead in the 23rd minute after pressing goalkeeper Josep Martínez into an error. Inter kept pressing, and Carlos Augusto cut the deficit in the 77th minute after Lautaro Martínez supplied the ball from the right. Thibaut Courtois protected Madrid’s lead with several key saves, including an 89th-minute stop from Henrikh Mkhitaryan, as Madrid held on in a match featuring 37 shots and 13 saves between the goalkeepers.

sports.title: Haaland double gives Manchester City 2-0 win at Porto
sports.summary: Erling Haaland scored in the 47th minute and again in stoppage time as Manchester City opened their Champions League league-phase campaign with a 2-0 win at Porto's Estádio do Dragão on September 8. The victory gave Enzo Maresca his first Champions League win as City head coach and three early points in the competition
sports.content: Erling Haaland scored in the 47th minute and again in stoppage time as Manchester City opened their Champions League league-phase campaign with a 2-0 win at Porto's Estádio do Dragão on September 8. The victory gave Enzo Maresca his first Champions League win as City head coach and three early points in the competition. Diogo Costa kept the match goalless before halftime, but Haaland headed in Enzo Fernandez’s cross shortly after the restart and finished from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s pass in the 90+1st minute. Tensions rose near halftime after Marc Guehi’s clash with Gabri Veiga; security staff became involved near the tunnel, and The Guardian reported that images showed Rúben Dias placing a hand on what appeared to be Porto coach Francesco Farioli.
